reason: The hypothesis synthesizes separate observations from multiple papers—phase-specific strain rate sensitivity (P6, P15), dynamic strengthening in eutectic HEAs (P3, P7), and local chemical order/dislocation interactions (P8, P12, P24, P28, P46)—into a single mechanistic framework of 'phase interface–mediated dynamic dislocation barrier formation' that none of the passages explicitly proposes. It links these elements through a mechanism that combines rapid dislocation pileup at interfaces with homogeneous deformation in the softer phase, and it designs a falsification test that directly compares intact vs. homogenized phase boundaries under dynamic loading, which goes beyond the individual studies.
copied_elements: eutectic/dual-phase HEA with lamellar L12 and B2 phases
phase-specific mechanical testing via micro-pillar compression
strain rate sensitivity comparison (quasi-static vs. dynamic)
homogenization heat treatment to alter phase boundaries
local chemical order/heterogeneities as dislocation obstacles
